criteria.text: Diagnosis of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a cardiologist or pulmonologist (approval criterion 1).
WHO Group 1 PAH confirmed by right heart catheterization (approval criterion 2).
Tried and failed a PDE5 inhibitor after 60 days OR currently taking a PDE5 inhibitor (e.g. tadalafil) (approval criterion 4).
Provider certifies patient is not pregnant and will not become pregnant while receiving Opsumit (approval criterion 5).
Baseline liver function tests (LFTs) submitted (approval criterion 6).
Baseline LFTs must not indicate moderate to severe hepatic impairment (denial criterion 2).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Opsumit (macitentan) Criteria Version 1; Original 12/27/2022; Approval 01/20/2023; Effective 03/01/2023.

Encoded: closed WHO Group 1 PAH indication, approval criteria 1-6, and denial criterion 2. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria. Current PDE5 inhibitor use has no minimum duration requirement; prior failure requires at least 60 days.

Cautions (notes only): contraindicated in pregnancy; monitor for pulmonary edema in patients with PVOD (pulmonary veno-occlusive disease); monitor LFTs throughout treatment as clinically indicated; avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir) or moderate dual CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inhibitors (e.g. amiodarone).
Duration (notes only): initial approval 6 months; reauthorization 12 months with chart notes indicating positive clinical response to treatment.
Quantity (notes only): #30 10mg tablets per 30 days. max_units is null; quantity is not evaluated.
Documentation verification, cautions, duration, reauthorization and quantity require manual review; this pack remains partial. Linked alternatives require their own criteria review.
